statement: In juvenile (13-24 day) rat barrel cortex regular-spiking glutamatergic neurons recorded whole-cell at 25.3 C with an ATP-free pipette, tolbutamide 500 uM raised Rm by a mean of 32 percent (17.7 percent in the 8 'responsive' of 9 cells) and depolarised by 2.8 mV (4.5 mV), and diazoxide 300 uM lowered Rm by 13 percent (26 percent in 8); the implied tolbutamide-sensitive share of control conductance is 16 +/- 8 percent (11 +/- 7 percent in 8) (percentages derived by me from per-cell source data; INFERENZA arithmetic; layers I-IV, not L2/3 only; ATP-free pipette may favour open KATP). [V4 correction: 'pyramidal-type' is unsupported: RS means glutamatergic regular-spiking and only 26 of the 63 RS cells are pyramidal by morphology in Fig 1 source data; 'rat' is not supported for the Fig 4 and Fig 2 cohorts (species not stated); 25.3 C is the cohort mean (per-cell 20.3-34.1 C, 38 of 277 cells above 30 C; per-cell temperatures of the Fig 2 and Fig 4 cells not tabulated). The resting-share estimate is INFERENZA: per-cell 1 - R0/Rtol gives 16 +/- 8 (SEM; SD 25, per-cell range -22 to +60, bootstrap 95% CI 0.9 to 32), 8 responsive cells 10.6, conductance-weighted 13.5-15.2, pooled 39 cells 13.0 +/- 2.7, Fig 2 voltage clamp (n 18) 12.9 by Rm and 15 as -6.6 pA over the +45 pA diazoxide current; probably an upper bound (ATP-free whole-cell; tolbutamide specificity for Rm untested in the knockout; Rm includes Ih); within the RS cells alone the share cannot be told from zero]
locator: Fig 4 source data 1 (per-cell Rm, Vm, firing, cell type RS); Fig 4A-J (viewed); Methods 'Whole-cell patch-clamp recording'

statement: KATP channels opened by diazoxide carry about half of the whole-cell conductance (RS G_KATP/G_total 0.52 +/- 0.08, n 7; 3211 +/- 1124 pS; reversal -101.7 +/- 5.0 mV near E_K -106.0 mV; pooled 63 neurons: Rm -270 MOhm), and tolbutamide reverses it; the paper does not give the resting share, and the diazoxide state is a ceiling for the channels that can open, not the number open at rest.
locator: Results 'Characterization of KATP channels'; Fig 2C-H (viewed); Fig 2 source data 2

statement: Kcnj11 knockout and ATP-free dialysis: KCNJ11 is the pore subunit in these neurons (WT outward 46.7 +/- 19.0 pA at -50 mV in 19 of 26 cells, knockout inward -59.9 +/- 11.9 pA in 20 of 22); with the ATP-undisturbed gramicidin recordings, 15 mM lactate (with 2.5 mM glucose) roughly doubled firing (209 +/- 49 percent), diazoxide cut it to 71 +/- 18, pyruvate acted like lactate, and the lactate effect was 147 +/- 25 percent in WT (n 9) versus 112 +/- 32 in Kcnj11-/- (n 10); the perforated-patch cells are not typed in the source data, so the pyramidal share of that result is not separable, and Vm and Rm were not reported. [V4 correction: the authors' caveat that the knockout inward current means other conductances were also altered is omitted; the Fig 5 workbook names 10 mM glucose as the 1.0 baseline where the row says 2.5 mM; printed +/- in the workbooks equal sd/sqrt(n-1) while the producer's derived values use sd/sqrt(n)]
locator: Fig 3, Fig 5 source data 1,3,4; Results last paragraph of 'Characterization...' and 'Enhancement of neuronal activity by lactate'

statement: Sada 2015 as reported by Karagiannis 2021 (second-hand): LDH metabolites including pyruvate and oxaloacetate can lead to KATP closure, and in Sada 2015 'intracellular ATP was found to be ineffective for reverting KATP channel opening induced by LDH inhibition'; the earlier SCI44 note that LDH inhibition opened KATP is therefore a citation inside a citation; Sada 2015 itself was not opened.

statement: KATP is not uniformly seen at rest in neocortical pyramidal neurons: a rat layer II-III pyramidal study reports no effect of diazoxide 3-300 uM or tolbutamide 300 uM on membrane potential or apparent input resistance (abstract only; age and temperature unknown), while rat layer II auditory-association pyramidal neurons (21-35 days, 33-34 C, 2 mM ATP in the pipette, TTX plus synaptic blockers) showed a glibenclamide 100 uM inward holding current of -26.4 +/- 3.8 pA at -60 mV (n 13) next to Ba2+ 500 uM -41.0 +/- 6.0 pA (n 8) and ML133 -21.5 +/- 3.8 pA (n 16) (currents, not shares), and immature entorhinal layer III pyramidal neurons responded to tolbutamide with 4 mM ATP in the pipette (firing only). [V4 correction: Lemak 2014 reports resting potential 'not affected by tolbutamide (n 12, p 0.397)'; 'P10-13 for most firing recordings' is not in the text (it is the field-potential age); hippocampal and neonatal items outside the perimeter: 16207875 (TASK in CA1 pyramidal cells), 9852317 (juvenile CA1 KATP), 16262667 (P0-4 layer V OGD, Rin fall)]

A K2P-type share cannot be stated for juvenile neocortical somata: the only neocortical pyramidal K2P-blocker panel read is dendritic, adult (injected at 8-12 weeks), chamber at 36 C (the 30 C of SCI43 D09 belongs to the Patch-seq paragraph; correction), and pools a broad cocktail that contains Ba2+ 1 mM with bupivacaine and QX-314, A1899 100 nM and fluoxetine 100 uM; dendritic membrane resistance rose 88.5 +/- 15.9 to 111.3 +/- 16.6 MOhm (+26 percent derived; n 11, 3 mice, P 0.004) and the legend does not separate the arms, so no K2P-selective share follows. [V4 correction: Source Data Fig 5f separates the arms (dendritic Rm: A1899 n 4 +8 percent; fluoxetine n 4 +44 percent; Ba2+ 1 mM cocktail n 3 +41 percent; pooled 88.47 to 111.35 MOhm); 'no K2P-selective share follows' stands; the claim that broad-tuft and slender-tuft neurons are pooled in 5f is unsupported (the text names broad-tuft neurons only)]
locator: Results 'DSDPs depend on the closing of leak K+ channels'; Fig 5d-g legend; Fig 5f (viewed); Methods dendritic recording
